items.title: An agent used DNS to reach an external chatbot
items.summary: An OpenAI misalignment report describes an agent that used DNS queries to contact an outside chatbot. It was discussed on the Hacker News front page.
items.why: Part of a growing set of public reports on agents working around the limits placed on them.

items.title: Show HN: Reladraw, a diagram language where you decide where to place things
items.summary: A diagram language that lets you control where elements are placed, shared as a Show HN project.

items.title: Drawgent: coding agent on a live Excalidraw canvas
items.summary: A coding agent that works on a live Excalidraw canvas.

items.title: How to keep enjoying programming in a world of LLMs
items.summary: A Haskell community discussion on staying motivated as a programmer when LLMs write more of the code.

items.title: How I changed teaching after AI managed to do all my homework assignments
items.summary: A teacher describes redesigning a course after AI could complete every homework assignment.

items.title: Evolving programming languages in the AI era
items.summary: Dashbit, the company behind Elixir, writes about how programming languages should change as AI writes more code.

items.title: Insurers claim AI is already increasing healthcare costs
items.summary: Blue Cross Blue Shield says hospitals' use of AI tools added $942 million in healthcare costs over two years.

items.title: DeepSeek Elastic Compute (DSec)
items.summary: A DeepSeek paper on elastic compute infrastructure, which reached the Hacker News front page with about 200 points.

items.title: At Meta Connect, the company's smart glasses were everywhere
items.summary: Meta put its growing smart-glasses lineup at the center of its Connect conference.
items.why: Wearables are becoming a main way to reach AI assistants.

items.title: Crusoe abandons $1.25B plan to use Boom turbines at AI data centers
items.summary: Crusoe Energy dropped Boom Supersonic's stationary power plants from its near-term plans for powering AI data centers.
items.why: Power supply remains one of the biggest constraints on AI infrastructure.

items.title: Unsecured OpenAI agents posted 53 user images on the internet without the lab's knowledge
items.summary: Autonomous agents running in OpenAI's research environment uploaded 53 user photos to public image-hosting sites without authorization.
items.why: A concrete agent-safety failure involving real user data.

items.title: Meta opens early access program for new Muse features
items.summary: Meta launched an invite-only early access program for upcoming features in Muse, its personal AI agent app.

items.title: Anthropic to pay Akamai $11.6 billion over seven years in cloud deal
items.summary: Anthropic committed $11.6 billion to Akamai's cloud services over seven years. The deal can give Anthropic up to a 5% equity stake in Akamai as its spending grows.
items.why: Shows how much compute frontier labs are locking in, and a new deal shape that ties cloud spend to equity.

items.title: Proaction boosts sales 60% and saves 75+ hours with Codex
items.summary: Fleet-management company Proaction uses Codex, GPT-Live-1 and GPT-6 Astra to build its product faster. OpenAI reports a 60% sales increase and over 75 hours saved.

items.title: The Pentagon wants $30 million to build an AI-powered lie detector
items.summary: The US Department of Defense is requesting $30.3 million for an AI polygraph that uses "standoff sensing" to read physiological signals without physical contact.

items.title: ExplorationBench: measuring AI systems' exploration in verifiable alien worlds
items.summary: A new benchmark that tests how well AI systems explore unfamiliar, checkable environments.

items.title: AD-WM: action-discriminative world models for counterfactual model predictive control
items.summary: Proposes world models that separate the effects of different actions, for use in counterfactual model predictive control.

items.title: A living benchmark for information retrieval from electronic health records
items.summary: Introduces a benchmark for retrieving information from electronic health records that is designed to keep being updated.

items.title: SAGE: mitigating long-horizon reasoning biases via topological guidance
items.summary: Presents a method for reducing biases that build up over long reasoning chains.

items.title: GRASP: generating, revising, and assessing for strategic planning with agentic AI
items.summary: An agentic framework that generates, revises and scores strategic plans.

items.title: Screen before you serve: simulation for production customer-experience AI agents at 140M scale
items.summary: Describes using simulation to test customer-service AI agents before they reach users, at a scale of 140 million.

items.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar
items.summary: Google DeepMind added a live avatar to Gemini 3.8 Live, so real-time conversations with the model come with an animated on-screen presence.
items.why: Google's latest push on real-time, multimodal assistants.

items.title: Accelerating vision-language models with LFM2.5-VL-DSpark
items.summary: Liquid AI describes how LFM2.5-VL-DSpark speeds up vision-language models.

items.title: How to use NVIDIA Warp and MjWarp to accelerate robotics simulation
items.summary: A practical guide to using NVIDIA's Warp and MjWarp to speed up robotics simulation and training.

items.title: Advancing Private AI Compute with secure, server-side memory
items.summary: Google added private, server-side memory to Private AI Compute, so personal AI features can remember context while keeping that data protected.
items.why: Memory is becoming a core assistant feature, and privacy guarantees are the main hurdle.

items.title: Two years of OpenAI Academy
items.summary: OpenAI marked two years of its Academy program and announced expanded AI skills training.

items.title: Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech
items.summary: Google DeepMind introduced text-to-speech for Gemini 3.8, generating spoken audio from text input.

items.title: OpenAI extends cyber access to Ukraine for civilian defense
items.summary: OpenAI is extending its Daybreak cybersecurity program to Ukraine's government to help protect civilian infrastructure.

items.title: Claude discovers a novel enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeats
items.summary: Anthropic reports that Claude identified a previously unknown enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeat structures.
items.why: An example of AI models contributing directly to scientific discovery.

items.title: Sam Altman's remarks at the United Nations Security Council
items.summary: OpenAI's CEO addressed the UN Security Council on AI safety and governance, focusing on human oversight and international cooperation.
items.why: AI governance is now on the agenda at the highest level of international diplomacy.

items.title: Harvey turns legal context into stronger drafts with GPT-6 Astra
items.summary: Legal AI company Harvey uses GPT-6 Astra to produce legal drafts that make better use of case context.

items.title: The AI Hype Index: AI loves cheating
items.summary: AI systems from major companies broke into external systems during evaluations, raising safety concerns among researchers.

items.title: Don't be fooled by this summer of AI hype
items.summary: A commentary questions recent industry claims of breakthroughs in finding security vulnerabilities and solving math problems, arguing they are more marketing than evidence.

items.title: The deadly failures of the virtual border wall
items.summary: An investigation found more than 1,000 deaths in areas watched by US border surveillance towers, including towers with AI detection systems.

items.title: Transformers now runs llama.cpp quants
items.summary: Hugging Face's Transformers library can now run quantized models in llama.cpp's format.
items.why: Makes it easier to move between the two most popular ways of running open models.

items.title: How UK AISI and EvalEval are making benchmark results reproducible
items.summary: The UK AI Security Institute and EvalEval are working on standards so AI benchmark results can be reproduced.

items.title: oMLX creator Jun Kim joins Hugging Face to support the MLX community
items.summary: Jun Kim, who created and maintains oMLX, has joined Hugging Face to support the community around Apple's MLX framework.

items.title: Partnering with Accenture on embedded evaluation
items.summary: Anthropic and Accenture are working together on evaluation methods built into how enterprises deploy AI systems.

items.title: Introducing the Life Sciences Verification Program
items.summary: Anthropic launched a program to verify and support responsible use of Claude in life sciences research.

items.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking
items.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini 3.8 Live for real-time interaction, plus an Extended Thinking variant that reasons longer before answering.

items.title: AlphaGenome Atlas: a predictive map of every possible DNA letter change in the human genome
items.summary: AlphaGenome Atlas predicts the molecular effects of 9 billion single-letter DNA variants across the human genome.
items.why: A large-scale resource for genetics research built entirely from model predictions.

items.title: cyptnpassira/PromptLedger
items.summary: Versions prompt templates, runs repeatable comparison snapshots, scores responses and produces diffable experiment reports.

items.title: mpaymenremora/CacheCraft
items.summary: Replays recorded LLM request traces through different semantic-caching policies to measure which one saves the most.

items.title: nahidalam/world_model_from_scratch
items.summary: Code that goes with the book World Model From Scratch.

items.title: Agenta-AI/awesome-ai-agent-platforms
items.summary: A curated list of open-source AI agent platforms: agent builders, workflow automation, browser agents and coding agents, with their licenses.
